$comment: Black halter crop top.  Round 2.  Heights and widths re-read off
ref/views/body_2.png with the metre grid keyed to the panel's alpha bbox
(sole = 0, hairTip = 1.715 -> 743.44 px/m) and the body centreline at
x = 195 px.  The centreline is confirmed by the choker, which is symmetric
about it: at y = 1.450 the dark wrap runs -0.048..+0.046 and at y = 1.440
-0.058..+0.062.  (The boots are NOT on that centreline -- their midpoint
sits ~32 mm to her right at 171 px -- so do not derive it from the feet.)
ROUND 1 DEFECTS FIXED HERE
1. The cut edge was a single plane, i.e. a straight oblique chord, and it
was 8..15 mm too wide over the whole ribcage.  Classifying the front
panel into skin / black cloth gives the cloth's outer edge, her right
(the side her arm does not overlap):
and her left, where the arm crowds it: .090 .090 .086 .079 .074 .067
.063 .065 .066.  Read the other way -- the highest cloth in each column
which agrees with the row scan to a pixel.  So the edge is a CURVE: its
slope is ~0 up to y = 1.30 and rises to 0.75 by y = 1.38.  `edge` is
that curve, a monotone-cubic table of half-width against height, and it
replaces armEdgeX/Y/Z/Slope.  The numbers in it are the plane constant,
not the silhouette: the z-tilt (armEdgeDepth) adds up to 38 mm at the
front, so the table is fitted against the baked shell, iterating on the
probe in out/top_probe.ts.
2. The neck strap was a slab of constant half-width 0.060 butted onto the
bib, so the neckline had a right-angle notch at (0.060, 1.375) -- very
visible at yaw 45.  `collar` is now a curve too, and it continues the
bib's silhouette (0.061 at 1.380 -> 0.052 at the top) instead of
stepping off it.  It is also offset by collarX, because the reference's
cloth span at the throat is not centred on the spine: -0.051..+0.062 at
the slab centred on x = 0 and the opening off centre at +0.016, her left
strap came out 5 mm wide -- a spike, not a strap.  Built, the straps are
3. The strap's top was a flat horizontal cut at y = 1.4315 that read as a
ledge.  It is now rounded (collarRound) AND lifted to 1.4365, inside
the choker's lowest wrap (1.4333..1.4437), with the cloth offset thinned
from 9 mm to 5.8 mm between y = 1.400 and y = 1.430 (neckThin*) so the
strap's outer radius there, 0.0430 + 0.0058 = 0.0488, clears under the
wrap's outer radius of 0.0499.  That is what the reference shows: the
straps run under the choker rather than stopping against it.
4. The brass keeper loop on the hem band was never modelled.  It is at
x = -0.048..-0.039, y = 1.231..1.251 on the sheet -- a 9 mm brass bar
wrapping the band, mirroring the steel buckle frame at +0.018..+0.046.
Built 12 mm wide because 9 mm is under one low-LOD voxel.
NECKLINE.  The opening is a rounded V that widens as it climbs, not a
constant-width slot, and it is off centre toward her left:
so neckOpenX 0.016, half-width 0.0125 at the bottom flaring at 0.60 and
clamped at 0.031 (above y = 1.4333 the choker covers everything anyway).
The cloth is one run at y = 1.380 (-0.059..+0.063) and two at 1.390, so
the scoop bottoms out at y = 1.3865.
HEM AND BAND.  The cloth's bottom edge is at y = 1.2246 at the centreline
and 1.2219..1.2259 out to |x| = 0.065, i.e. flat, not the 1.218 round 1
used.  The band's seam is at y = 1.250, so the band is 1.2240..1.2495.
The reference's band edge is at |x| = 0.101, the same as the bib's, so
underBandProud comes down from 8 mm to 3 mm.
LACING.  Re-checked, unchanged.  Brass eyelet centres off the brass mask:
cluster spans x -0.052..+0.049 and y 1.300..1.372.  The built cross spans
laceThick/ringThick are NOT the reference's thicknesses, they are the depth
needed to survive the mesher: at 5 mm the diagonals fall under one low-LOD
voxel and the X bakes as an H.
BACK.  clay_5 / body_5 show a bare upper back, skin from the shoulders down
to the band.  backZ0/backSlope bite that opening out of the bib only; the
collar is exempt, because the halter's strap really does ring the neck --
body_5 has a dark band at the nape at y = 1.44.
PROXY.  The garment hangs on a copy of body.ts's trunk and it has to stay a
copy: in round 1 the copy had drifted -- it still expected body.trap to be
a capsule (x0/y0/z0..) when body.ts had made it an ellipsoid (cx/cy/cz,
rx/ry/rz), so the proxy silently dropped the trapezius altogether -- the
shoulder mass that reaches x = 0.099 at y = 1.420 where the yoke column on
its own is only 0.053, a 46 mm hole in the surface the collar hangs on --
and it
used a hand-written bust and a smootherstep loft where body.ts uses
body.bust and a Fritsch-Carlson one.  Fixed here.  If body.yoke, body.trap,
body.bust or body.blend* move, this moves with them.
BUDGET.  voxelScale was 0.68 in round 1: a 3.1 mm voxel at --lod high and
62.7 k triangles, 12% of the whole character's budget for one garment.
0.80 is 3.6 mm / 44.7 k, and the X lacing still reads at the low LOD's
8.4 mm voxel because paint() carries its colour even where the mesher
rounds the ridge off.
